REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JUNE 13, 2019 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

This section is reserved for comments related to Consent Calendar Items and items not listed on the Agenda but within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council/Successor Agency. Comments are limited to 5 minutes per person.
7.
Consent Calendar
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the City Council/Successor Agency, there will be no separate discussion of these items unless a Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.
7A.
Approval of Minutes
Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of May 21, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of May 23, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

Public Hearings
8A.
Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A JOINT RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY, APPROVING AND ADOPTING THE ANNUAL BUDGET FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020, APPROPRIATING THE FUNDS NECESSARY TO MEET THE EXPENDITURES SET FORTH THEREIN, AND APPROVING THE INVESTMENT POLICY FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020 FOR THE CITY OF CERRITOS AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

Review and consideration of adoption of the Fiscal Year 2019-2020 appropriation limit.
Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING AND ADOPTING THE ANNUAL APPROPRIATION LIMIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020 (COUNCIL).

Review and consideration to renew the Municipal Law Enforcement Services agreement by and between the County of Los Angeles and the City of Cerritos for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2024 (COUNCIL).

10A.
Report on pending legislation.
10B.
Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.
11.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
JUNE 13, 2019, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Jeff Ludington, Generations Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos Recreation Services Division Teen
  Volunteers – Preethi Narayanan and Somto Eze.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  None.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Tyler Harris announced his candidacy for President.

  Ernie Nishii spoke regarding a recent event related to the dangers of “vaping.”

  Case Vander Linden spoke regarding street maintenance and submitted a document for
  the record.

  Mel Cortez requested the City institute social media sites.

  Herman requested library card vouchers for the homeless and the exercise of first
  amendment rights.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum spoke regarding first amendment rights.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of May 21,
  2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of May 21, 2019
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7A.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  May 23, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of May 23, 2019
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated June 13, 2019
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  6/13/2019  $8,734,528.98 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.2. Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos
  Redevelopment Agency dated June 13, 2019 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  Successor Agency  6/13/2019  $1,850.00 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  June 13, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 6

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A JOINT RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY
  TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY, APPROVING AND ADOPTING THE
  ANNUAL BUDGET FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020, APPROPRIATING THE FUNDS
  NECESSARY TO MEET THE EXPENDITURES SET FORTH THEREIN, AND APPROVING
  THE INVESTMENT POLICY FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020 FOR THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT
  AGENCY (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  Staff reports were given by Jeff Thielke, Budget Manager, Mike Matsumoto, Financial
  Consultant, and Gary Caporicci, representing the City’s auditors, The Pun Group. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Herman expressed concern as to budget deficits.

  Mel Cortez expressed concern regarding subsidizing the enterprise funds with the
  general fund and suggested cost reductions and revenue enhancement
  measures.

  Jay Gray expressed concern regarding the budget position, raising resident fees,
  costs for operation of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts and Magnolia
  Power Plant, and City Treasurer position.

  Case Vander Linden expressed concern regarding street maintenance.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum spoke regarding parking in the community and suggested
  uses for City facilities.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  the public hearing and public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to make the
  following adjustment in the final Fiscal Year 2019-2020 annual budget as related to
  City Council employee benefits (Code 111, Account No: 52400): Reduce from
  $100,200 to $89,500 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to make the
  following adjustment in the final Fiscal Year 2019-2020 annual budget as related to
  City Council travel and meetings (Code 111, Account No: 53080): Reduce from
  $50,000 to $20,000 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  June 13, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 6

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  MOTION (DID NOT PASS): It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Hu, to table
  the budget consideration to a future meeting date (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR
  AGENCY).

  The motion did not pass (2 - 3) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Solanki
  NOES:  Edwards, Pulido, Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Receive and file Planning Commission Resolution No. PC 2019-17, finding the
  Capital Improvement Program for Fiscal Year 2019-2020 in conformance with
  the General Plan for the City of Cerritos; and

  2. Waive full reading of and adopt Joint Resolution No. 2019-11 and CSA
  2019-1, A JOINT RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS
  REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY, APPROVING AND ADOPTING THE ANNUAL
  BUDGET FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020, APPROPRIATING THE FUNDS
  NECESSARY TO MEET THE EXPENDITURES SET FORTH THEREIN, AND
  APPROVING THE INVESTMENT POLICY FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2019-
  2020 FOR THE CITY OF CERRITOS AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE
  CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY), as
  amended to include the following two (2) adjustments as approved by previous
  City Council action:

  a. City Council employee benefits (Code 111, Account No: 52400): Reduce
  from $100,200 to $89,500
  b. City Council travel and meetings (Code 111, Account No: 53080): Reduce
  from $50,000 to $20,000; and

  3. Direct staff to present items for City Council consideration throughout Fiscal
  Year 2019-2020 relative to revenue enhancement and cost reduction options
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (3 - 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Yokoyama
  NOES:  Hu, Solanki
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of adoption of the Fiscal Year 2019-2020 appropriation
  limit.

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING AND ADOPTING THE
  ANNUAL APPROPRIATION LIMIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020 (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  June 13, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  A staff report was given by Jeff Thielke, Budget Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Herman spoke regarding various propositions as related to budget allocations.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to waive full reading of
  and adopt Resolution No. 2019-12, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING AND ADOPTING THE ANNUAL
  APPROPRIATION LIMIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Edwards, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration to renew the Municipal Law Enforcement Services
  agreement by and between the County of Los Angeles and the City of Cerritos for
  the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2024 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Herman referred to the components in the proposed agreement.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Approve the Municipal Law Enforcement Services agreement by and between
  the County of Los Angeles and the City of Cerritos from July 1, 2019 through
  June 30, 2024; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Municipal Law Enforcement Services
  agreement by and between the County of Los Angeles and City of Cerritos
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Edwards, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None.
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  June 13, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 6

10.  Legislative Items

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, and Hu, Pulido, Mayor Pro
  Tem Yokoyama and Mayor Solanki.

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Direct staff to return with information for the City
  Council’s consideration related to the prohibition of vaping in public facilities,
  including the golf course, prohibition of sales of vaping products, and to
  reconsider the prohibition of smoking at all City facilities, including the golf
  course.

12.  Closed Session

  The City Council did not recess to Closed Session and did not discuss Agenda Item
  12A.

12A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957(b) (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney Services

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 10:39 p.m. in memory of former Mayor and City
  Councilmember John Crawley.
